To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduction of an antimicrobial management program was associated with a pseudo-outbreak of hospital-acquired infections.

a pseudo-outbreak of hospital-acquired infections occurred in an acute care hospital in the USA after implementation of an antibiotic control programme, and the pseudo-outbreak was due to a change in clinical documentation of hospital-acquired infection.

an abrupt and persistent 3-fold increase in the rate per 1000 patient-days of nosocomial pneumonia, bloodstream infection, urinary tract infection, and other nosocomial infection was associated with the start of an antibiotic management program and was not caused by an outbreak.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a pseudo-outbreak of hospital-acquired infection.
the effect of antibiotic stewardship on nosocomial infection rates.
the development of a new method of detecting and preventing the spread of nosocomial pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was no outbreak of nosocomials, and that the apparent outbreak was due to a change in documentation.
the nosocomial infections were not due to an outbreak of infection, but rather to a change in the way clinicians documented nosocomial infection.
the nosocomial infections reported during the period of May to December 1998 were a pseudo-outbreak.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a pseudo-outbreak of 30% nosocomial infection was detected at our institution.
a pseudo-outbreak of infections can occur when clinicians are asked to justify existing antibiotic practices after the implementation an antibiotic management programme.

an abrupt increase in the nosocomial rate was associated with the implementation of an aggressive antibiotic management programme and that the apparent increase was due to a change in the threshold at which clinicians reported nosocomial infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clinicians should document nosocomial infections based on clinical criteria and not on their perception of what the infection control practitioner expects.
clinicians may alter their documentation practices in response to an antibiotic management programme in an attempt to justify their antibiotic prescribing practices.
a pseudo-outbreak of infections is a possibility and should be considered when investigating nosocomial infection outbreaks.
